newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain backs Madrid airport expansion, not new one.
newsitem.headline: Spain backs Madrid airport expansion, not new one.

text.p: Spanish Development Minister Rafael Arias Salgado said on Thursday he backed an expansion of Madrid's airport Barajas to relieve overcrowding rather than the construction of a second airport.
"The best possibility for Spain, not just for Madrid, is the full expansion of the Barajas airport," Salgado told Spanish national radio.
"If we begin now to build a second airport and leave Barajas as it is, Spain would stop being one of the key centres of world air transport."
According to Salgado, a Barajas expansion would be the best solution for air traffic control as well as for the Spanish national airline Iberia.
Barajas has a great future as a distributor of European air traffic to southern Africa and Latin America, he said.

Although the addition of a fourth, or a fifth, runway would produce noise pollution problems for neighbours, Salgado said Spain was spending 16 billion pesetas ($112 million) in noise protection for those most affected by the third runway, now under construction.
Should environmental concerns block further Barajas expansion, Salgado suggested the next most viable option would be to use the nearby Torrejon de Ardoz airport facilities.
Only if this too proved unfeasible should a second airport, which would take some 10 years and cost at least one trillion pesetas, be built.
"We don't have time for a second airport," Salgado said.
